I'm 51 years old, been farming these 16.9 mu in Quzhou for 35 years. My old man taught me, and I've learned a thing or two since. I finished middle school, so I can read those extension leaflets they hand out at the ag shop, but honestly I trust what I've seen with my own eyes more than what some young technician tells me. It's just me and my wife at home now — our child works off-farm in Shijiazhuang. So labor's tight when things get busy, and money's always tight too. Every yuan I spend on inputs has to be weighed against what we need for living expenses.

Right now it's early spring, the wheat I sowed last October is starting to green up. I got all 16.9 mu in wheat-maize double crop — that's the only system that makes sense here. Last year I got about 420 kg per mu on the wheat, decent but not great. This year I'm hoping for 450 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

For the wheat that's in the ground now: I already put the base fertilizer down at planting — about 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu. The extension guy says I should topdress 25 jin of urea per mu at jointing, but I think 20 jin is enough. That's about 10 kg of nitrogen in the topdress, so total nitrogen for the season is around 18 kg per mu. If the wheat looks yellow and weak at green-up, maybe I'll add a little more, but 20 jin has worked fine for me in most years. I'll irrigate three times: once at green-up, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. Each time I pump water it's about 25 yuan per mu — costly, but dry wheat means shriveled grains, and that hurts worse than the pumping bill. I sprayed herbicide last fall, but if I see weeds in the spring I'll spray again. Maybe fungicide too if the weather turns wet and warm.

After wheat harvest in early June, I got maybe five to seven days to get the maize in. I can't mess around with deep tillage in that window — I'll just clear the wheat stubble with the rotary tiller and plant directly. I buy hybrid seed from the ag shop in town, usually costs about 55 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, I'll put down compound fertilizer in the row at planting, about 40 jin per mu, then topdress with urea at the big trumpet stage when the plants are knee-high — about 30 jin per mu. Total nitrogen comes to around 16 kg per mu for maize. I'll irrigate twice: once right after planting to help germination, and once at tasseling if it hasn't rained. Maybe a third time if it's really dry, but I'll play that by ear.

Labor is mostly me and my wife, but at wheat harvest I'll hire the combine — it's 50 yuan per mu plus I need someone to help haul the grain. For maize harvest I'll probably hire a couple of day laborers for three days, that's 150 yuan per day each. Total input costs for the year will run about 13,000 yuan. That's a big chunk of our savings, but I'm not going to under-fertilize to save a few hundred — a bad yield costs far more than a bag of urea. Still, I don't have money to waste, so I'm sticking with what I know works.
